required_outcomes: Notices that the email arrives the day after the job was closed on Riverside's report that the door lock was fixed and tested on 29/04, and that it does not say whether the fault came back after the repair.
Asks Leo a short, specific question: has the door stopped closing again since the engineer's visit on 29/04, and if so since when.
Does not dispatch anyone, raise a new paid job or seek landlord approval until Leo answers, and sets a dated follow-up for his reply.
acceptable_alternatives: Alerting Riverside Compliance at the same time that a return visit under their repair may be needed, without booking it.
Reopening the closed job pending Leo's answer rather than raising a new one.
positive_behaviours: Tells Leo that if the repair has failed, the original engineer will be asked to come back.
Notes on the job that the email may be a late or resent message.
red_flags: Treating the email as a new fault and seeking fresh landlord approval for a new paid call-out.
Escalating to a human over an unclear one-line email.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a provider or booking a visit before the fault is confirmed.
Approving or recording any further payment on this job.
critical_failures: Ignoring the email because the job is closed, so a possible failed repair goes unchecked.
